correctness.rationale: The graph is finite connected unweighted d-regular bipartite, endpoint classical RK4, with an explicitly bounded weighted regular extension. Writing q=dh, P=A/d, the Taylor coefficients of f(q(I-P)) are nonnegative for 0<=q<=1. Every noncomplete connected bipartite graph has a distance-three opposite-class nonedge, giving exact transition (q³/6)(1-q)(P³)_{uv}, permanently negative when q>1. Complete K_{d,d} spectral projectors give cross-class (1-f(2q))/(2d) and positive diagonal/same-part entries, hence cutoff q=1.3926467817..., which also equals the stability endpoint since L has maximum eigenvalue 2d. Verified C6 distance-three at h=3/5 exactly -9/625, with 2h=6/5<ρ; algebraic signs and extension normalization are consistent. The finite example is only corroborative.
